subject: ClearCloud SLA: uptime floor & monthly credit carveout
messages:
From: Megan Li <megan.li@clearcloud.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: ops@clearcloud.com
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: SLA ask: uptime floor + monthly credit carveout

Hi Soojin —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal and ops teams reviewed the standard SLA you shared and we have two requests before we move to procurement:

1) Uptime floor: we need an explicit 99.95% monthly uptime commitment for the production inference endpoint (regional). The current template lists 99.9% as a baseline.
2) Maintenance carveout: for scheduled maintenance windows related to model upgrades, we need a defined monthly carveout (4 hours/month) that does NOT count toward uptime calculations, and a corresponding reduction in credits if maintenance is pre-announced.

If the uptime moves to 99.95% we understand that remedy caps / monthly credits will change — can you share a proposal with the adjusted credit bands and an example calculation for a 30-day month? I attached the redlines our procurement team suggested.

We are targeting a decision by end of week so procurement can raise the PO next Monday.

Thanks,
Megan
Megan Li
Director, Cloud Ops — ClearCloud
megan.li@clearcloud.com

Attachment(s): ClearCloud_SLA_Redlines_v1.pdf (referenced)
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Megan Li <megan.li@clearcloud.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 12:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask: uptime floor + monthly credit carveout

Hi Megan —

Appreciate the clear asks and the redlines. Summarizing how Redwood can meet you partway and the operational impacts:

- Uptime: we can offer a regional production commitment of 99.95% for the pinned model endpoint under a Dedicated capacity or Reserved-hosted plan. That shift increases maximum monthly credits; see attached "MonthlyCreditsTable.xlsx" for new bands.
- Maintenance carveout: we can formalize a scheduled maintenance carveout of up to 4 hours/month per region if announced 72 hours in advance. Pre-announced maintenance will be excluded from uptime calculations; unscheduled emergency maintenance will still count toward uptime unless we mutually agree otherwise.

Key tradeoffs / asks from our side:
- Remedy cap: to keep economics predictable we propose a remedy cap of 30% of monthly invoice for any single month when uptime breaches occur (vs. the unlimited / uncapped ask).
- Rollout pinning: to keep the 99.95% commitment, the customer must pin the model version for the month (we'll support canaries but full version switches in production are considered configuration changes and may impact SLOs).

I attached an updated draft SLA (SLA_Draft_ClearCloud_v2.pdf) that incorporates the 99.95% wording, the 4-hour maintenance carveout, and the credit table. If that looks okay, I can ask our contracts team to produce a DocuSign link — cc'ing Ben and Laura so we can turn around any legal redlines quickly.

Next steps:
- Megan: confirm the carveout terms and whether ClearCloud will pin to a model version monthly.
- I'll circulate the DocuSign if you confirm, and Ben/Laura will triage redlines.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Attachment(s): SLA_Draft_ClearCloud_v2.pdf; MonthlyCreditsTable.xlsx
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: internal: quick redline notes on 99.95% ask

LAURA / SOOJIN —

Quick internal note before we send for signature: I reviewed the v2 and have two small asks from legal/finance — both for the Draft we send to ClearCloud:

1) Add explicit language limiting credit stacking across regions and accounts. If they run multi-region instances, remedies should be per-account-per-region, not aggregated.
2) Clarify maintenance notification window: 72 hours is OK, but require that scheduled maintenance windows be limited to 2 occurrences/month unless agreed.

These are lightweight and keep exposure bounded. I can draft the exact phrasing; want to avoid a re-open during procurement. If you both approve, I'll put those redlines into the DocuSign wrapper.

-ben
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Ops — Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: SLA ask: uptime floor + monthly credit carveout

Hi Megan —

Thanks for the review and for the rapid turnaround on procurement timing. We made the legal clarifications Ben suggested and have produced the updated agreement. Key confirmations below: 

• Uptime commitment: 99.95% monthly regional uptime for the pinned production inference endpoint (applies when ClearCloud elects Reserved-hosted or Dedicated capacity).
• Maintenance carveout: 4 hours/month scheduled maintenance excluded from uptime, 72-hour announcement required, limited to 2 scheduled windows/month.
• Remedy cap: monthly credit cap is 30% of invoice for the impacted region (credits calculated per-account-per-region).
• Model pinning: to retain the uptime commitment customer must pin the model version for the billing month; canary testing allowed in isolated traffic slices.

I pushed the final DocuSign link here: https://docusign.com/clearcloud/sla/CLR-2027-0456 — please route to your procurement team. Once signed we will finalize onboarding dates and the Reserved capacity start date.

If you'd like a short call to run through the credit table and example calculations I can make time tomorrow morning.

Warmly,
Laura Bennett
VP, Contracts — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
